Article Title: Bankipur bypoll: Prashant Kishor adds a dash of yellow to Bihar palette of saffron & green
Article Text:
Jan Suraaj party workers celebrating Prashant Kishor's victory





PATNA: Bihar has been green. It has been saffron. Now Prashant Kishor brings yellow.Kishor, architect of poll victories for others, has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as Jan Suraaj broke through BJP’s saffron and RJD’s green duopoly.Born in Rohtas in 1977, Kishor studied in Buxar, completed his Class XII from Patna Science College, earned a BBA from Lucknow University and a master’s in healthcare management from ASCI, Hyderabad. He did a French language course in France before spending eight years in a UN-supported public health programme.National prominence came after helping design PM Modi’s successful 2014 LS campaign. His organisation, I-PAC, went on to work with multiple political parties. He advised former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee and parties across Punjab, Andhra and Tamil Nadu, earning a reputation as one of the country’s most successful political consultants.After helping the Nitish-led Mahagathbandhan win in 2015, Kishor briefly joined JDU before returning to grassroots politics.A self-professed believer in Gandhi’s philosophy, he spent nearly two years on a padayatra across Bihar before launching Jan Suraaj Party on Oct 2, 2024. Its candidates drew a blank in the 2025 state polls, raising questions over whether his campaign skills could translate into votes.Barely eight months later, the answer arrived in Bankipur. Defeat would have dealt a crushing blow to both Kishor and Jan Suraaj. Instead, victory fuelled debate over whether Bihar has room for a third political force.“I did not contest to become an MLA or turn Bankipur into a metropolitan city like Bengaluru,” he said. “I wanted to send a message to BJP brass — generate employment, provide education and stop migration, or be prepared for similar results.”Married to Dr Jahnavi Das and father to a son, Kishor lives like a monk on campaign. He rarely watches TV news, hasn’t used a laptop in a decade, and relies only on his phone to stay connected with his grassroots network.
Article Summary: Prashant Kishor, architect of poll victories for others, has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as Jan Suraaj broke through BJP's saffron and RJD's green duopoly.

Article Title: Congress vs Congress in Punjab: With 'sleeper cell' warning, party puts Channi camp on notice
Article Text:
Baghel and Warring warned of action against "sleeper cells" amid Congress's escalating feud with former CM Channi

Congress message for Charanjit Singh Channi?

Channi from 'chosen one' to ‘dissident’

Why Congress is backing Warring

So, what should be the way forward?

NEW DELHI: Will the Congress crack the whip against dissidents in Punjab? With differences between state president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi becoming an embarrassing public spectacle, the Congress has sent out a strong message to disgruntled leaders in Punjab, warning of action against "sleeper cells" within its own ranks in the poll-bound state."We have to identify and fight the sleeper cells inside the Congress. A strong organisation at the booth level is the key to victory," said AICC general secretary and Punjab in-charge Bhupesh Baghel, in a clear message to those who have raised a banner of revolt against the leadership. Baghel declared that the Congress was fighting a "multi-cornered battle" not only against political rivals but also against those within the party allegedly working for opponents.Taking forward Baghel’s message, state Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring declared that no party ticket would be given to anyone found operating as part of "sleeper cells." "While the high command will decide the candidates, I will ensure that no person working against the party gets a ticket. Loyalty to the Congress is non-negotiable," the Punjab Congress chief asserted.Warring also targeted former state Congress chief Sunil Jakhar, who is now with the BJP, accusing him of betraying the Congress during the 2022 assembly elections.Warring alleged that Jakhar had worked in tacit understanding with the BJP despite heading the Congress campaign committee.While Baghel and Warring did not take any names, their target was obvious. The dissidents in Punjab are backing former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi, who has been unhappy after being denied the post of state Congress chief in the organisational reshuffle that was announced on July 1. The move triggered a storm that continues to rock and embarrass the party even a month later.With Warring retained as state Congress chief by the party high command, Channi and his supporters have missed no opportunity to show their “dissent” and openly challenge the party’s decision. Even the presence of Baghel in the state has not helped to ease tempers. From poster war to sloganeering at party meetings - here’s how the open show of defiance has played out.While "Go Back Baghel" poster surfaced in Muktsar, another poster surfaced in Ferozepur showing Channi wearing a vest with "RSS" printed on it.Supporters of Channi have indulged in sloganeering at party programmes attended by Warring and Bhupesh Baghel in Patiala and Sangrur.In another event in Sangrur town, activists of both camps clashed in the presence of senior leaders.Channi's camp, comprising several state leaders, has been demanding the replacement of Warring by citing specific instances on how the state chief had created divisions within the party leadership.Last month, they even gave an open ultimatum to the central leadership to make Channi, the Congress MP from Jalandhar and a prominent Dalit face, as state chief saying that under Warring's leadership the Congress cannot come to power.Interestingly in 2022, Channi was the chosen one as the Congress grappled with intense internal fighting between the then chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh and his challenger Navjot Singh Sidhu.With the two senior leaders engaging in open power tussle, Congress sidelined both and picked Channi to lead the state and the party in the 2022 assembly elections. But under Channi, the Congress was decimated and reduced to 18 seats from the 77 it had won in 2017 under Captain Amarinder Singh.Channi, who has now been made the head of the Congress campaign committee, has dropped enough hints that he does not accept the leadership of Warring.And that brings us to the present Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, who was handed over the reins of the party by Rahul Gandhi in 2022 after the humiliating defeat in assembly elections.Warring, who has faced sloganeering from supporters of Channi during recent party programmes, has refused to step down. He has said that if the party high command decides to replace him, he would continue to work to strengthen the organisation."I have no desire to be the chief minister. I will better retire than leave the Congress. Rahul Gandhi also knows that Raja Warring can die, but never compromise with the BJP," he said in one of his speeches.Warring has cited Congress’s 2024 Lok Sabha performance - when it won seven of 13 seats - to justify his efforts at reviving the party.In a highly emotional speech at his hometown in Muktsar recently, Warring had said: "Everyone is after my life. Akalis, BJP and the broom (AAP) and even some of our own are after me. I have not committed any sin and my only sin is that when we came from 80 to 18 I was handed over the reins of the party."Maintaining that he started from the scratch when the morale of the party's rank and file was low and some leaders preferred to stay abroad for months together, Warring said he led from the front.Warring played down the slogans raised by Channi's supporters during party events and said, "People oppose those who are successful. Those 20-25 poor souls who come, one doesn't even know how they are brought in or what they are told. I actually feel sorry for them; this sort of thing has been happening for ages. The event went well; people listened to the speeches, and there was a huge crowd. People do these things; it doesn't matter. I have been in politics for 25 years."Former Punjab minister Razia Sultana called upon the party high command to take strict action against all those who were indulging in indiscipline and damaging the party. She warned that if timely action was not taken, the party could suffer major damage."Nip the evil in the bud," Sultana remarked.But can the Congress do that? Theoretically yes, but practically we haven’t seen the grand-old-party take clear leadership decisions, except perhaps in Karnataka. For the Congress high command, the standard playbook for handling leadership tussles in states has been “ambiguity is the best policy.”And Punjab has been no different. One can only hope that the Congress acts before it is too late. The strong warning to dissidents is a welcome first step, but it remains to be seen if the party high command can follow this up with action without being scared of the consequences.
Article Summary: Congress warns of action against "sleeper cells" amid feud with former CM Channi. State president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring and former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi are locked in power tussle. Supporters of Channi have indulged in sloganeering at party programmes.

Article Title: Kolkata opens its doors after 19 years: Where does Taslima Nasreen go next?
Article Text:
Taslima Nasreen

Homecoming: Delayed, but not denied

Dwikhandito

Kolkata: Then and now

Where to next?

Lajja

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For 19 years, Taslima Nasreen carried Kolkata in her memories, longing to return but unable to do so. The city that had become her “second home” after she left Bangladesh in 1994 remained out of reach. Forced to flee her country of birth and later compelled to leave the city where she had settled, Nasreen spent much of the past three decades moving from one place to another, not in search of adventure but of refuge, without quite recovering the sense of home she associated with Kolkata.That door finally opened nearly 19 years late r.Nasreen set foot in the City of Joy on July 31 and received a civic felicitation at Rabindra Sadan on August 1. The visit was accompanied by a warm official welcome from West Bengal’s new government, with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari assuring the writer of security whenever she chose to visit.The author, who was forced to leave Kolkata in 2007, responded with gratitude. “It’s not just the city I return to; for me, it’s a homecoming to a lost chapter of my life,” she said.The change of government has given Nasreen fresh hope of spending more time in Kolkata, something that did not become possible under the previous two administrations. But it has also raised a more difficult question: Is her return merely a ceremonial visit, or could it be the first step towards once again making Kolkata her home?In November 2007, Kolkata witnessed violent protests by groups opposed to Nasreen and her writings, including her memoir. Amid concerns over her safety and the worsening law-and-order situation, the authorities moved her out of the city.She was taken first to Jaipur and later kept under security in New Delhi before eventually leaving India for Europe. Her repeated appeals to successive governments to let her return to Kolkata did not produce a result.Almost two decades and two changes of government later, her return became possible. “Taslima Nasreen’s return proves that Bengal is in good hands now. Threats and intimidation are in the past. Every pillar of the Constitution and fundamental rights are safe now,” Adhikari said at the felicitation.“You can come to Kolkata whenever you want, as many times as you want, and stay as long as you want . As the chief minister and police minister of Bengal, I am personally responsible for your security.” Nasreen was equally effusive in her gratitude.“History remembers who shut the door. Now, history will also remember who reopened it,” she said. “The opening of this door proves injustice can feel like a long night, but it’s never permanent.” But the cordial exchange also opened a larger conversation.Can Kolkata become a sanctuary to which Nasreen returns not merely as a guest but as a long-term resident? The answer is not straightforward. The chief minister can assure her of security within the state, but any longer-term residential arrangement would also depend on her visa status and decisions by the appropriate immigration authorities. Visa extensions and residential permits for foreign nationals are handled through the FRRO/FRO system and, in some cases, the Union home ministry.Nineteen years is a long time, particularly in a period of rapid political and social change. The Kolkata Nasreen knew in the early 2000s is not the city to which she has returned.For the writer, “every year in banishment looked like a door heavily bolted”. Meanwhile, although the government that moved her out of the city is no longer in power, her return has acquired a new and complicated political context.Nasreen has not forgotten how abruptly she had to leave Kolkata while the Left Front governed Bengal. She remains sharply critical of the Left, accusing sections of it of failing to defend free-thinkers while claiming to stand for secularism and progressive values.But the Kolkata of 2026 is governed by the BJP, and Nasreen’s return unfolded amid the symbols and slogans associated with its politics. Chief Minister Adhikari was welcomed at Rabindra Sadan with chants of “Jai Shri Ram”, a religious invocation that has also become a prominent political slogan.Nasreen has consistently argued that religion and the state should remain separate.“Humanity has to be bigger than any doctrine,” she said during her homecoming address.She also sought to draw a clear line between gratitude and political endorsement. “I’m thankful to this government for letting me return. But my gratitude doesn’t warrant my allegiance to them. I haven’t come here for any political party,” she said.The question, therefore, is not whether she is grateful to the government that facilitated her return. She plainly is. The harder question is whether Kolkata can protect her right to disagree with the same establishment if her views become inconvenient to it.The cultural composition of the felicitation offered another indication of how much the city’s public life has changed. For a ceremony honouring one of the Bengali language’s most internationally recognised writers, relatively few prominent members of the literary fraternity were present.Novelist Shirshendu Mukhopadhyay, who had been expected to attend, was absent. Poet Joy Goswami was present, but his appearance led to the most uncomfortable moment of the evening.When Nasreen invited Goswami to join her on the stage, a section of the audience erupted in protest, shouting slogans and objecting to his presence on the dais. Goswami, who had begun walking towards the stage, turned around and returned to his seat.The disruption continued for several minutes. Nasreen waited quietly before appealing to the audience to calm down and allow the programme to continue.The irony was difficult to miss. An event organised to celebrate a writer who had spent decades defending freedom of expression had briefly become a venue for preventing another poet from speaking.The hostility appeared to be connected to Goswami’s perceived proximity to the previous Trinamool Congress establishment and criticism that prominent cultural figures had not done enough to defend Nasreen when she was made to leave Kolkata. Whatever the political grievance, however, it could not justify denying him the opportunity to speak after Nasreen herself had invited him.Goswami did not confront the protesters and later left Rabindra Sadan without reading the poem he had written for Nasreen.“Everyone has the right to speak. When someone speaks about freedom of expression, people support it; but when a poet is invited to speak, they do not want to hear him. That is not right,” Nasreen said the following day.“It wasn’t just Joy who was insulted. I was also insulted because I had invited him.”The organisers also expressed regret over the incident. Nasreen subsequently spoke to Goswami by telephone after being unable to visit him during the trip.The episode showed how quickly cultural spaces can become arenas for political resentment. For all the celebration surrounding Nasreen’s homecoming, Kolkata is still negotiating the same difficult questions about dissent, ideological loyalty and the right to disagree that formed the background to her departure.The real test will not be how warmly the city welcomes her when her presence suits the political moment. It will be whether Kolkata continues to defend her when she says something those in power, or their supporters, do not wish to hear.Kolkata has reopened its doors to Nasreen after nearly 19 years. Her own homeland, however, remains out of reach. Afterprovoked widespread outrage among Islamist groups, Nasreen faced threats and criminal proceedings over her writings and public statements. Her Bangladeshi passport was revoked, and she left the country in 1994.Nearly 32 years later, she has still not been able to return permanently. Exile remains the defining condition of her life. “The number of years I’ve been away from home has already surpassed the sum of time I was allowed to live there,” said Nasreen, who will turn 64 later this month.And yet she has supported former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina’ s right to return to the country, even though Nasreen has said that Hasina’s government opposed her own attempts to return to Bangladesh in 1999. “I’ve criticised Sheikh Hasina in the past,” Nasreen said. “The ban on the Awami League must be revoked since it’s undemocratic. Sheikh Hasina wants to return. I want her to return for the sake of democracy in Bangladesh.”Hasina, who has been living in India since her government fell in August 2024, has said she intends to return to Bangladesh by December despite a death sentence handed down in absentia, which she rejects as politically motivated. She was scheduled to make her first public appearance since her ouster through a virtual address in New Delhi on August 5.Nasreen’s defence of Hasina’s right to return is notable precisely because of their history. It is an argument that the right to go home should not depend on political sympathy or personal gratitude. “No one wants my return. Sheikh Hasina did not. Neither did Khaleda Zia nor those who came to power subsequently,” Nasreen said, her disappointment over the repeated refusals unmistakable.But she refuses to abandon hope. “It took me 19 years to be able to say, ‘Kolkata, I’ve come back to you’,” she said. “I have tears in my eyes, but I come with a heart full of love.”Her return to the City of Joy has renewed her belief that seemingly permanent barriers can eventually fall. “Nineteen years stand between my exile and return. But the opening of this door proves injustice can be long-standing but never permanent.”Perhaps that is why Nasreen continues to dream of a day “when no writer has to live in exile from her own country”. She hopes Bangladesh will one day separate religion from the state and become a country where women have equal rights, minorities can live with dignity and free-thinkers and non-believers are not threatened for their views.In India’s neighbouring country, that day may yet come. For now, Nasreen is grateful that she can at least return to Kolkata, revisit its familiar spaces and, she hopes, attend the Book Fair as she once did.Her former address in the city no longer belongs to her. Kolkata has changed, and the pet that once helped make the city feel like home is no longer alive. But after nearly 19 years, Taslima Nasreen has returned, carrying with her hope, unfinished arguments and, perhaps, a few more lives in reserve.
Article Summary: Taslima Nasreen returned to Kolkata on July 31 and received a civic felicitation at Rabindra Sadan on August 1. The writer was forced to leave the city in 2007 amid concerns over her safety and the worsening law-and-order situation. The change of government has given Nasreen fresh hope of spending more time in the city.

Article Title: Lok Sabha secretariat director found hanging in Noida flat; suicide note recovered
Article Text:
Lok Sabha secretariat director found dead at Noida flat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A director in the Lok Sabha Secretariat allegedly died by suicide at his flat in a Noida housing society, police said on Wednesday.The deceased, identified as Gaurav Gautam, was found hanging from a ceiling fan in his apartment at Kendriya Vihar-II Society in Noida's Sector 82 on Sunday, police said, as cited by PTI.Police said a purported suicide note recovered from the flat referred to a loan. Its contents are being examined as part of the ongoing investigation.According to the Phase-2 police station, officers were alerted to the incident after receiving a memo from a hospital, where Gaurav Gautam had been taken. Doctors declared him dead on arrival.Police said Gautam's wife had gone to her parental home. On returning, she found the flat locked and, sensing that something was wrong, entered the apartment with the assistance of a security guard.She found Gautam hanging and immediately rushed him to a nearby private hospital, where doctors declared him dead, police said.A forensic team and local police later inspected the scene and collected evidence. After completing the inquest proceedings, the body was sent for a post-mortem examination.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha secretariat director found dead at Noida flat. Gaurav Gautam was found hanging from a ceiling fan in his apartment. Police said a purported suicide note recovered from the flat referred to a loan. Its contents are being examined as part of the ongoing investigation.

Article Title: Meet Brock Lesnar’s family: All about his wife Sable, his parents, siblings, children, and the strong family support behind the retired WWE superstar
Article Text:

Who is Brock Lesnar’s wife Sable?

Who are Brock Lesnar’s children?

Who are Brock Lesnar’s parents and siblings?

Brock Lesnar may be known as one of the most dominant names in WWE history, but away from the spotlight, he is a dedicated family man. The retired WWE superstar has been married to former WWE star Sable for nearly two decades, and together they have built a private life focused on raising their children.While fans remember Lesnar as “The Beast Incarnate”, his biggest role today is being a husband and father. From his famous wife to his talented children and the parents who raised him on a South Dakota dairy farm, here’s a closer look at the family behind one of professional wrestling’s biggest legends.Brock Lesnar’s wife is Rena Marlette Lesnar, better known to wrestling fans as Sable. She became one of WWE’s biggest female stars during the late 1990s and early 2000s. Besides wrestling, she also worked as a model and actress before stepping away from the spotlight.The couple first met while working in WWE. At the time, Sable had returned to the company, and their relationship soon became serious. They got engaged in 2004 and married in 2006. Nearly 20 years later, they are still together.In his autobiography, Lesnar explained that he wanted to prove how serious he was about their relationship after they stopped talking for a while.He eventually surprised Sable at her home, stayed with her for several days, and later proposed in a romantic setting near a waterfall.Lesnar also shared that he wanted both of them to leave WWE if they planned to build a long-term future together. He believed the demanding lifestyle and physical toll of the business were not ideal for a healthy family life. Sable retired from WWE in 2005 and has stayed away from wrestling ever since, while Lesnar now has also retired from WWE.Brock Lesnar is the father of four biological children and is also a stepfather to Sable’s daughter.He shares sons Turk and Duke with Sable. Both boys chose hockey instead of wrestling and have already played at competitive levels in Canada.Before marrying Sable, Lesnar welcomed twins Mya and Luke with his former fiancée Nicole McClain. Mya Lesnar has become one of the top college shot put athletes in the United States. She won NCAA indoor and outdoor championships and continues to impress with record-breaking performances. Her twin brother Luke has followed his father’s path into wrestling and has won multiple state wrestling titles.Sable also has a daughter, Mariah, from her first marriage. Together, the family has largely stayed away from public attention despite Lesnar’s worldwide fame.Brock Lesnar was raised by his parents, Richard and Stephanie Lesnar, on a dairy farm in Webster, South Dakota. Life on the farm was tough and demanded discipline from an early age. Lesnar has often credited his hardworking parents for helping shape the mindset and determination that fueled his success in wrestling. His father, Richard Lesnar, passed away in 2019 due to heart-related complications. Brock also has two brothers Troy and Chad and a sister named Brandi.
Article Summary: Brock Lesnar is the father of four biological children and is also a stepfather to Sable’s daughter. He shares sons Turk and Duke with Sable. Mya Lesnar has become one of the top college shot put athletes in the United States.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “They never really cared or ever talked about medal placement, podium placement, none of that” How Simone Biles’ family helped her chase greatness without pressure
Article Text:
How Simone Biles’ family helped her chase greatness without pressure(Getty)

Inspiring story of the day by Simone Biles:

“They never really cared or ever talked about medal placement, podium placement, none of that.”

The real story behind Simone Biles’ message about medals and success

How Simone Biles’ parents created a champion without chasing medals



“I think that’s why I have been so successful,” Biles said while explaining the impact of their approach.

How Simone Biles’ family helped her stay grounded through fame

How Simone Biles overcame Tokyo heartbreak with her family beside her

How Jonathan Owens supported Simone Biles during her Paris comeback

What Simone Biles’ journey teaches about success

Before Simone Biles became one of the greatest gymnasts in history, her parents gave her a lesson that had nothing to do with winning. Ronald and Nellie Biles never built her childhood around medals, rankings or expectations. They wanted her to enjoy gymnastics, stay happy, and understand that her value was never tied to the results of a competition.Biles has credited that approach as one of the reasons she was able to handle the pressure that came with becoming an Olympic champion. While speaking at the World Business Forum in New York, she said, “They never really cared or ever talked about medal placement, podium placement, none of that."The sports world knows Simone Biles as a record-breaking athlete; her parents always saw her as their daughter first. Their support helped her develop the confidence to compete freely, even when expectations became impossible to ignore.When Simone Biles said her parents “never really cared or ever talked about medal placement, podium placement, none of that,” she was explaining the mindset they built from childhood.Ronald and Nellie Biles never ignored her ambition or told her that winning did not matter. Instead, they made sure medals were never the only measure of success. Their focus was on her happiness, safety and love for gymnastics.Before competitions, their message was simple: “Good luck, have fun, be safe.”Those words allowed Biles to compete without the fear of disappointing anyone. Even as expectations grew after her Olympic success, she continued trusting the process instead of letting pressure control her. That lesson became even more important during the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, when Biles stepped away from events to protect her mental health. Her parents had already taught her that she was more than her performances.The message behind her quote was never about caring less about winning. It was about chasing greatness while remembering that a medal does not define a person.Simone Biles’ journey started long before the Olympic podiums. As a young gymnast, she had the talent to become special, but her family made sure success did not come with unnecessary pressure. Ronald and Nellie Biles focused on creating stability and balance. Instead of asking about scores after competitions, they cared about how she felt and whether she enjoyed the experience.For Biles, those simple gestures carried more meaning than any motivational speech. They reminded her that her parents supported her regardless of the outcome.That viewpoint allowed Biles to chase greatness without fearing failure. She still wanted to win and trained relentlessly, but she never believed a medal was the only thing that defined her.That balance helped her become a dominant force in gymnastics. Biles won four gold medals and one bronze at the Rio 2016 Olympics, became the most decorated gymnast in World Championship history and introduced skills that changed the sport forever. However, the foundation behind those achievements was created at home.As Simone Biles’ career grew, her parents made sure that success never completely changed her life. They understood that gymnastics required commitment, but they also believed family time was a must. Biles has spoken about how her parents insisted on taking vacations even when training demands increased.Those breaks allowed her to spend time with family and step away from competition. For Ronald and Nellie, those moments were part of helping their daughter grow. They wanted Simone to have memories outside the gym and avoid feeling that her entire life depended on gymnastics.Even after becoming an Olympic champion, Biles said her parents continued treating her normally. She once joked that medals did not protect her from household responsibilities: “They didn’t care if I won whatever medals. I wasn’t immune to anything, not the dishes,” Biles said.“My dad, if you ask him, he still doesn’t understand whenever I go and do stuff like this,” she said, referring to her speaking appearance at the forum. “He’s like, ‘People want to see my daughter? Why my daughter? It’s just Simone.’”That simple example showed how her family helped her stay grounded. They celebrated her achievements but never allowed fame to change their relationship.The importance of that support became clear during the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. Biles entered the Games as the biggest name in gymnastics, with the world expecting another historic performance. Instead, she faced one of the toughest moments of her career. During the competition, Biles experienced the “twisties,” a situation in which gymnasts can lose awareness of their bodies while performing skills in midair. Because continuing could have been dangerous, she stepped away from several events and focused on her mental health.The decision created worldwide discussion. Some criticised her, while many athletes supported her honesty. In Biles' case, the choice was about safety and understanding herself.Her family’s support became more important than ever because they reminded her that she was more than gymnastics. When Biles returned for the Paris 2024 Olympics, she was not trying to prove critics wrong. She was competing with a better understanding of herself. She won three gold medals and one silver medal in Paris, completing one of the greatest comebacks in Olympic history.While Simone Biles’ parents shaped her mindset from childhood, her husband Jonathan Owens became another source of support during her return to the Olympic stage. At the 2024 Paris Olympics, Biles admitted she even felt nervous before major moments. During the individual all-around final, after a difficult uneven bars routine, she looked toward Owens in the stands to regain her focus.Biles later explained the importance of having her loved ones around her. “I look at them in the audience to soothe me. It’s a stress buster.”Owens’ presence reminded Biles that she had support beyond gymnastics. For her, those moments were not about medals or pressure, but about having people around who helped her stay calm and confident.Simone Biles’ journey is not only about medals and records. It is about having people who allow you to grow without fear.Her parents gave her the freedom to chase greatness without making her feel trapped by expectations. They showed her that success could exist alongside happiness and balance. Jonathan Owens supported her during one of the biggest moments of her career, just as her family had supported her through every challenge before.Today, Simone Biles remains one of the greatest athletes in history. But the mindset that helped her reach the top was created long before the Olympic medals arrived.It began with a simple message from her parents: "Good luck, have fun, be safe.”Those words helped Simone Biles become a champion while never losing herself.
Article Summary: Simone Biles’ parents never ignored her ambition or told her that winning did not matter. Ronald and Nellie Biles focused on creating stability and balance. Their message was simple: “Good luck, have fun, be safe”

Article Title: "This is Candace's Satan": Candace Owens faces fresh backlash after viral post accuses her of targeting innocent people over her latest Charlie Kirk investigation claims
Article Text:
Candace Owens is facing renewed criticism after a viral X post accused her of dragging innocent people into her coverage of the Charlie Kirk investigation and promoting conspiracy theories. The criticism came as Owens addressed claims involving Frank Turek, saying viewers could judge his remarks for themselves, while previewing updates about Officer Bagley and Alan Robertson. The exchange has fueled fresh debate over her reporting style and the evidence behind her claims.

Candace Owens draws criticism after viral social media post

Candace Owens responds to Frank Turek controversy and investigation claims

Candace Owens is once again at the center of an online storm after a viral social media post criticized her recent commentary and accused her of repeatedly expanding the list of people linked to the ongoing Charlie Kirk investigation. The post gained traction as Owens released a new video addressing claims involving Christian apologist Frank Turek, while also teasing fresh updates connected to Officer Bagley and Alan Robertson.The latest debate erupted after an X post from the account Cinema Shogun sharply criticized Owens' recent content. The post claimed her latest episodes had become increasingly sensational and accused her of repeatedly pointing fingers at new individuals instead of narrowing the focus.The post also alleged that Owens had suggested Frank Turek was encouraging violence against her, while claiming she had continued introducing new names into discussions surrounding Charlie Kirk's death. It further argued that innocent people were being dragged into online speculation, with critics warning that such claims could expose individuals and their families to harassment.The criticism quickly spread across social media, where users debated both Owens' reporting style and the growing influence of commentary-driven investigations.While some agreed with the criticism, others defended Owens' right to ask questions and pursue stories she believes deserve public attention.The exchange has added another chapter to the already heated online conversation surrounding Owens, whose recent broadcasts have regularly generated intense reactions from supporters and critics alike.As discussion around the viral post intensified, Owens addressed the controversy in a video shared with her audience.She said:"Okay, so Frank Turek is trending. People think that he's kind of calling for me to be killed. I'll let you guys be the judge of that. He's using biblical analogy, you know, doing the the thing that they always do where they're like, this is what happens in the Bible and this is Candace's Satan. It's a little much. People don't like it. I certainly could not get away with it if the shoe was on the other foot. And I was saying that stuff about Erika. ""Also, we get to solve another mystery for Officer Bagley. I can answer a question that he was unable to answer despite 10 months of having the ability to review footage. We have an update for you as well regarding Alan Robertson. We were hit with a ton of emails regarding his time in San Bernardino and we can clarify some matters now. A lot's going on on the show today. It feels like Turning Point is kind of coming apart. They sound very angry at a strange story about what happened at UVU campus the day before that nobody's talking about. "Her remarks suggested that she believes criticism directed at her differs from the standards applied to others. She also previewed additional discussion involving Officer Bagley, Alan Robertson and developments she said would be covered during her program.The latest exchange highlights how the Charlie Kirk investigation continues to generate fierce online debate, with competing narratives playing out across social media. While Owens continues to frame her broadcasts as an effort to answer unanswered questions, critics argue that public accusations should be supported by verified evidence before individuals become part of the conversation. As the debate grows, attention remains fixed on both the claims being made and the evidence presented to support them.
Article Summary: Candace Owens is facing renewed criticism after a viral X post accused her of dragging innocent people into her coverage of the Charlie Kirk investigation. The criticism came as Owens addressed claims involving Frank Turek, saying viewers could judge his remarks for themselves. The exchange has fueled fresh debate over her reporting style and the evidence behind her claims.

Article Title: 'Respect senior players': Ajinkya Rahane sends big message to Gautam Gambhir amid Test struggles
Article Text:
Ajinkya Rahane, Virat Kohli (left), and Gautam Gambhir

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India batter Ajinkya Rahane has said the Indian Test team needs to bring back the fight and patience that once defined its success, as he reflected on the team's recent struggles in the longest format.Rahane, who recently retired from international cricket, made the comments during his first podcast appearance since retirement. While India have won two ICC trophies in white-ball cricket under head coach Gautam Gambhir in the last two years, the Test team has struggled, including two home series whitewashes. India are currently fifth in the World Test Championship standings and are trying to qualify for the final.Rahane, who last played a Test in 2023, said Test cricket demands character and the ability to survive difficult periods.“Because I haven’t been playing Test cricket for the last two years, I’ve been sitting at home, watching the Indian team lose matches even in India as well. I think Test cricket needs character. You need to build such characters and play competitive cricket. That’s what’s important. Playing session out. You don’t see many teams do that. I don’t want to pinpoint any team, but you want to see people play out those tough sessions,” Rahane said on the Stick to Cricket podcast.India will begin a two-Test series against Sri Lanka in Galle on August 15.Rahane also spoke about Gambhir, with whom he shared the dressing room as a player, but said Test cricket has always been about handling difficult sessions.“I have played with him [Gambhir]. I was not with KKR when he was the coach. I never played under him when he was the coach. We played together when we came here [in England], and even in India. But I feel Test cricket is always about playing sessions, seeing out tough moments.”Rahane also pointed to the rapid transition in the Indian Test side. Within six months, India lost Ravichandran Ashwin, Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli from the Test setup. Without naming anyone directly, he said a Test team needs more experienced players alongside youngsters.Among the current squad, only Ravindra Jadeja, KL Rahul, Rishabh Pant and Jasprit Bumrah have played 50 or more Tests.“Test cricket fans are actual cricket lovers. What we built apart from the last two years when new players came in Test cricket, I still feel Test cricket needs 7-8 senior players and 2-3 younger players. What we are seeing now is that all the players are actually new. There’s hardly any senior cricketer left. So, Test cricket needs that,” Rahane added.He also admitted he is concerned about the future of the format.“Frankly, yes I do (fear for Test cricket). Because the way it is going, we all want Test cricket to survive, to be there – India, England, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa. These 4-5 teams specially. Because what I have seen in the last 2-3 years, you need to keep and respect the senior players, especially because with the Indian team, all the senior players going out together at once, that’s been the issue.”
Article Summary: Ajinkya Rahane says Indian Test team needs to bring back fight and patience. Rahane made the comments during his first podcast appearance since retirement. India have won two ICC trophies in white-ball cricket under Gautam Gambhir in the last two years.

Article Title: 'I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan': Arshad Nadeem blames Glasgow cold for CWG poor show

Pakistan’s Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem has blamed the cold Glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the Commonwealth Games. The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds, saying the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.Nadeem managed 77.41 metres with his second throw after opening with a foul. His third attempt was 75.39m, leaving him outside the top eight.“The weather was extremely cold and I personally felt that it affected my body. As you have seen in many of my previous competitions, my run-up is usually very smooth, but this time it wasn’t… because my body had become stiff due to the cold conditions. My fitness was good and my health was fine, but ultimately whatever Allah wills is what happens,” he told reporters on Wednesday.Despite the result, Nadeem said he remains determined to make a strong comeback and urged fans to continue supporting him.“Please don’t lose heart and don’t stop supporting me either. Whatever I have achieved has only been possible because Allah blessed me with the opportunity to do it. The respect and recognition Pakistan has received around the world have come through years of hard work. I worked tirelessly while staying in Pakistan,” he added.“God willing, I will prepare with full dedication for the upcoming competitions and once again raise Pakistan’s flag on the international stage.”Nadeem also responded to criticism on social media, saying he understood the disappointment among Pakistani fans.“I have heard many things on social media, but I want everyone to remember that I am Pakistan’s son, and I always will be,” he maintained.Nadeem’s next challenge will be the Lausanne Diamond League in Switzerland on August 21. He will face a strong field that includes India’s Neeraj Chopra , Commonwealth champion Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, Keshorn Walcott, Anderson Peters and Thomas Rohler.Nadeem will hope to regain his form before the Asian Games later this year.
Article Summary: Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem has blamed the cold Glasgow weather for his disappointing performance at the Commonwealth Games. The defending champion finished ninth after failing to make the final three rounds. He said the low temperature made his body stiff and affected his usually smooth run-up.

Article Title: Tokyo E-Prix round-up: All the biggest moments from Formula E's thrilling night race

Tokyo E-Prix 2026

Big blow for Formula E title contenders

First Formula E night race in Tokyo

The 2026 Tokyo E-Prix had everything Formula E fans could ask for. There was rain, changing track conditions, a first-ever night race in Tokyo, a surprise winner, a new championship leader and a manufacturers' title celebration. Mahindra Racing's Nyck de Vries produced a brilliant drive to win the race after starting fifth, while the title battle took another dramatic turn with just two races left in the season.Nyck de Vries delivered one of his best performances of the season to claim victory for Mahindra Racing. Starting from fifth on the grid, the Dutch driver handled the mixed weather conditions perfectly and worked his way into the lead.Citroen Racing's Nick Cassidy finished second, while Andretti Formula E's Jake Dennis completed the podium in third place.The race proved costly for championship rivals Pascal Wehrlein of Porsche Formula E and Mitch Evans of Jaguar TCS Racing. Both drivers failed to score any points, hurting their title hopes.Dennis made the most of the opportunity and moved to the top of the ABB FIA Formula E Drivers' World Championship standings with only two races remaining this season.While the drivers' title race remains open, Porsche Formula E celebrated after securing the 2025/26 ABB FIA Formula E Manufacturers' World Championship.The Tokyo E-Prix created history by hosting the city's first-ever Formula E night race. Fans packed the circuit to witness the unique spectacle under the lights. The event also attracted several well-known guests, including Princess Yoko of Mikasa, model and entrepreneur Lori Harvey, actor Melvin Gregg and fashion designer Shinsuke Takizawa.Olympians Yuki Ota, Laura Nolte and Adam Ammour were also present, along with Japanese TV presenter Ohshima Rinon, local racing star Juju Noda and former Formula E world champion Stoffel Vandoorne. One of the biggest moments away from the main race came when Japanese racer Juju Noda drove a GEN3 Evo Formula E car. It was the first time a Japanese driver had driven a Formula E car on home soil.Japanese music group One or Eight entertained fans with a live performance before the race, adding to the festive atmosphere.Special guests enjoyed exclusive access to Formula E's inner workings during the race weekend. They watched the race start from the Jaguar TCS Racing garage and followed qualifying sessions from the Andretti Formula E, Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E and DS Penske Formula E garages, getting a close look at the teams in action.The Tokyo E-Prix also featured the KYOJO CUP's special 'World Appearance & EV Kart Trial' programme. Female drivers competed in an EV kart time trial on a 600-metre circuit and took part in a driver introduction and award ceremony. The programme showcased Japan's women's motorsport scene and supported Formula E's focus on diversity and developing future talent.Also read: Nyck de Vries on winning Tokyo E-Prix Round 15: “We were a little bit lucky today”
Article Summary: Mahindra Racing's Nyck de Vries won the 2026 Tokyo E-Prix. Nick Cassidy finished second, while Andretti Formula E's Jake Dennis completed the podium. Porsche Formula E celebrated after securing the 2025/26 ABB FIA Formula E Manufacturers' World Championship.

Article Title: BCCI to standardise Bronco, 2K base fitness test parameters after England tour debacle
Article Text:
Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana

BCCI pulls up lacklustre fitness tests

Communication breakdown

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Injury prevention lost priority

NEW DELHI: Flustered by the frequent injury breakdowns of players in the Indian team, the medical team at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru is looking to resurrect its fitness programme. TOI understands that the CoE is finally working on standardising base fitness parameters after it emerged that the non-definitive customised fitness tests for players were identified as a core reason for the drop in the overall fitness standards.The Indian team went through a change in fitness testing drills after Adrian Leroux replaced Soham Desai as the strength and conditioning coach last year. It is learnt that the BCCI medical team, which includes the CoE and the Indian team, has struggled to work in sync to assess the fitness of players. Since Leroux took over, it was decided that the Bronco test would be the primary test to judge fitness instead of the Yo-Yo test.The Bronco test, which is a more agility driven test, didn’t have a base parameter till now. TOI has learnt that the BCCI medical team has rolled out a figure of 5.15-5.20 minutes as a base figure to complete the assorted drills to be declared fit enough to be selected after the debacle in white-ball tour of Ireland and England.Earlier, the BCCI had set 16.5 as a marker to clear the basic Yo-Yo test. The CoE has also set 9-10 minute mark to complete the 2 km running test which is known as the 2K test.“The Indian players are not used to the Bronco test. Over the last year, the CoE had set different base parameters for players. It has now emerged that certain senior players were given much comfortable targets to meet to clear fitness tests. The CoE staff had also cleared players like Harshit Rana and Nitish Kumar Reddy to make sure it was delivering players according to team management’s needs,” a BCCI source told TOI.TOI has learnt that the team management and BCCI, led by secretary Devajit Saikia, has questioned Team India physio Kamlesh Jain for the repeated breakdowns and overall dip in the fitness standards. The team management is also not happy with players cramping so frequently even in the favourable English weather.“Kamlesh has been told that he shouldn’t worry about any player’s stature and flag anything that he doesn’t find satisfactory. It has been seen that the mobility of some of the players in the field has been questionable. Senior batters are struggling to push their running between the wickets as they bat longer. The number of slow fielders has increased,” the source said.It has been observed that regular India players have not been prepared for the new fitness drills. For instance, someone like Mohammed Siraj was recently caught off guard by the sudden fitness tests at CoE before leaving for Sri Lanka.“It is only now that contracted players have been handed the base parameters of the new tests. The Test regulars were caught off guard by the programme given to them at CoE. The players who are not part of the Test team are now starting to work according to the base parameter,” the source said. The CoE failed to get Jasprit Bumrah ready despite the selectors and the team management were assured that he would be fit for the first Test in Sri Lanka on Aug 15.In the case of Harshit Rana, which has been an embarrassment for the CoE since he had just recovered from a knee injury, there was no clear messaging about the desired fitness levels. TOI understands that Rana had suffered severe cramps and not any injury when he was sent back to the CoE from England after the third T20I. It was cited that he was overweight.“The Indian team management flagged that he was overweight by four kgs. The CoE should have been much more vigilant. He has been now told by CoE staff that his weight can’t exceed 96 kgs. He is now 94 kgs and is expected to be cleared next week. But he was 97 kgs when he was cleared to be picked for the Indian team for the UK tour,” the source said.The Indian team management had finally got it right when it managed to play three consecutive ICC events — the 2023 ODI World Cup, 2024 T20 World Cup and 2025 Champions Trophy — with all resources available. Only Hardik Pandya suffered an injury after twisting his ankle in the 2023 World Cup. BCCI had devised an impeccable injury management programme and customised for each player.TOI understands that the fitness programmes have drifted away from prevention to a more rigorous approach. “Now, a player at CoE is made to take a 2K test and Bronco test more frequently besides the Yo-Yo test which burns out players. Earlier, it was about maintaining certain fitness marks for players without burning them out with fitness regimes. Yo-Yo tests were designed to be taken in six months or if a player is coming back from injury. The other management had made notes of pressure points for each player and accordingly regulated the workload. Now, the players are just pushed to do extreme fitness programmes,” the source claimed.
Article Summary: The medical team at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru is looking to resurrect its fitness programme. The CoE is finally working on standardising base fitness parameters after it emerged that the non-definitive customised fitness tests for players were identified as a core reason for the drop in the overall fitness standards.

Article Title: Gianni Infantino promised Morocco 2030 World Cup final in exchange for support, says report
Article Text:
FILE - FIFA President Gianni Infantino looks on during the women's Premier League match between Al Ahli FC and Al Ittihad FC at the Al- Ahli Club stadium in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, Thursday, Dec 14, 2023. (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez, File)

The Times

Report claims Morocco was offered the final

FIFA rejects the allegations

Pressure continues to build on Infantino

Morocco remains one of FIFA president's closest allies

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Times

The Athletic

Gianni Infantino's efforts to contain the growing crisis surrounding his FIFA presidency have reportedly taken another dramatic turn, with claims that he offered Morocco the right to host the 2030 FIFA World Cup final in exchange for political backing as pressure over his leadership continues to mount.The claim was first reported by, which said Infantino allegedly made the offer as he sought public backing from member associations ahead of next year's FIFA presidential election. Morocco is set to co-host the 2030 World Cup alongside Spain and Portugal, although FIFA has yet to decide where the final will be staged.According to The Times, Infantino has sought to strengthen support for his expected re-election campaign by privately assuring Morocco that it would stage the 2030 World Cup final.Morocco will co-host the centenary tournament alongside Spain and Portugal, while Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay will each host one commemorative opening fixture. However, FIFA has not yet selected the venue for the final.The report claims Morocco hopes to stage the match at the under-construction Hassan II Stadium near Casablanca after reports that Infantino has privately assured Moroccan officials they would host the 2030 FIFA World Cup final.Once completed, the 115,000-seat venue would become the largest football stadium in the world. Spain, meanwhile, is also pushing to host the final, with the renovated Santiago Bernabéu widely viewed as its preferred venue.FIFA has strongly denied the report, insisting that no commitment has been made over the location of the 2030 World Cup final.A FIFA spokesperson said: "It is false and misleading to claim the FIFA President has made any promise in relation to hosting the FIFA World Cup 2030 final. A decision will be made by FIFA in due course."Even if such assurances had been made privately, any future decision on the final venue would still require FIFA approval and could ultimately be revisited under a different administration.The latest report comes just days after Infantino abandoned the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal following widespread opposition from football's governing bodies and member associations.The project would have created a commercial entity to manage FIFA competitions, including plans to sell a minority stake in the World Cup to private investors. The proposal triggered fierce criticism from UEFA, the English FA, CONCACAF and several national associations before FIFA confirmed it would not proceed.Since then, UEFA has formally warned FIFA of potential legal action over the failed proposal, while calls for governance reforms and leadership changes have continued to grow.Morocco has been one of Infantino's strongest supporters since he became FIFA president in 2016.The FIFA chief has spent recent days in Rabat, where he reportedly convened an emergency meeting with senior officials at FIFA's Africa regional headquarters as the fallout from the failed FFE proposal continued. Rabat also hosts FIFA's regional office and is scheduled to stage the FIFA Congress in 2027.According to, Infantino has been seeking public declarations of support from member associations as he attempts to stabilise his position ahead of next year's presidential election.Recent reporting by Adam Crafton ofindicated that while several European associations have withdrawn their backing, countries including Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Lebanon and Kuwait continue to support Infantino's bid for another term, with Morocco and Egypt also remaining among his key allies.With FIFA denying the latest allegations and no official decision yet taken on the 2030 final venue, the contest over both the World Cup's biggest match and the organisation's future leadership is set to remain firmly in the spotlight.
Article Summary: Morocco set to co-host the 2030 World Cup alongside Spain and Portugal. FIFA has yet to decide where the final will be staged. Infantino allegedly made the offer as he sought public backing from member associations ahead of next year's FIFA presidential election.

Article Title: ‘He should go. Now’: Luis Figo unleashes bombshell rant tearing apart embattled FIFA boss Infantino
Article Text:
Luis Figo launches brutal attack on Infantino and demands he leaves FIFA/Image: AP, EFE

Figo launches extraordinary attack on FIFA president

Claims extend beyond the failed investment proposal

Pressure continues to mount on Infantino

"He should go. Now."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Luis Figo has called on Gianni Infantino to step down as FIFA president, delivering one of the strongest public attacks yet on the embattled football chief as the fallout from the collapsed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal continues to deepen.The former Portugal captain, who has served as a UEFA football adviser since 2017, accused Infantino of putting personal interests ahead of football and insisted the FIFA president could no longer salvage either his position or his reputation after abandoning the controversial plan to sell minority stakes in FIFA's flagship competitions to private investors.Figo's intervention comes as Infantino faces mounting pressure from national associations, football confederations and senior figures within the sport following the collapse of the proposal, which reportedly would also have seen him assume a senior executive position carrying an annual salary of around $30 million.In a statement published by the Daily Mail, Figo accused Infantino of attempting to push through sweeping changes to world football without properly informing FIFA's members, while suggesting the project would have primarily benefited the FIFA president and those close to him."Nothing gets in the way of pleasing his friends," Figo said, before describing Infantino's conduct as "the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed."The 2000 Ballon d'Or winner questioned why FIFA's leadership had not openly presented the proposal before member associations gathered for the World Cup final."If it was such a good idea, why not tell your members when you had them all in a room before the World Cup Final?" Figo asked."If it was such a robust plan, why not tell your members the risks as well as what you describe as the benefits?"He also referenced reports that Infantino was set to become chief executive of the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise."If the scheme was a no-brainer, why not be honest about the fact that it was going to give you a $30m-a-year job at the end of it?" Figo continued."But none of this was done. Because it's not a good idea. It's not robust when you fail to be transparent about the crippling returns that private equity always seek."Figo suggested the failed World Cup investment scheme was only part of a much broader pattern under Infantino's leadership.The former Barcelona, Real Madrid and Inter Milan star—who made nearly 800 club appearances during his career, earned 127 caps for Portugal and has worked as a UEFA football adviser since 2017—said he could write "10,000 words" about the problems at FIFA before listing several examples he believes have damaged the governing body's credibility."It's not bold when you fail to explain that once you have sold your share it is gone forever and you have disinherited your successors from ownership of the World Cup," he said."And it's not honest when you fail to mention that, after you have delivered the head of the World Cup on a platter to your mates in DC, they are going to give you a job worth five times your current salary."He then broadened his criticism beyond the FFE proposal."None of this comes as a surprise when you consider the litany of abuses he has inflicted on football's reputation," Figo said."From suspending and reversing disciplinary decisions to breaking the laws of the game over a half-time show, nothing gets in the way of pleasing his friends."Figo's comments add to the growing pressure surrounding Infantino after FIFA withdrew the FFE proposal following widespread opposition from across the football world.In recent days, senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigned, FIFA chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said staff had been "deceived", while FIFA's chief of global football development Arsène Wenger stated that scrapping the proposal was "absolutely necessary and beyond question."Potential successors have also begun to emerge behind the scenes, with CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani among the figures linked with a possible challenge should Infantino's presidency come to an end.Figo concluded his statement by arguing that the controversy had permanently undermined Infantino's leadership and that remaining in office would only cause further damage to world football."This plan, like the Super League before it, was blown apart by the media exposing every devious twist and turn before its advocates had their messaging straight. And thank goodness it was," he said."Infantino has debased the office of FIFA President that he promised to elevate. He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve.""He has lost the support of his senior staff, his closest advisers, the vast majority of people who devote their lives to this sport and even, it would seem, the FIFA Peace Prize winner."Figo ended with his clearest message yet to the FIFA president:"It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now."
Article Summary: Luis Figo calls on Gianni Infantino to step down as FIFA president. Former Portugal captain launches one of the strongest public attacks yet on the embattled football chief. Figo accuses Infanino of putting personal interests ahead of football.

Mackenzie Dern reached one of the toughest moments of her UFC career at UFC 295. On Nov. 11, 2023, she suffered the first knockout loss of her MMA career when Jéssica Andrade stopped her in the second round at Madison Square Garden.At that point, Dern’s journey toward UFC gold looked uncertain. She had already faced setbacks against some of the division’s top fighters, but the Andrade defeat became a major test. Instead of letting that loss define her, Dern rebuilt herself and eventually reached the top of the strawweight division.Mackenzie Dern entered UFC 295 looking to continue her comeback after defeating Angela Hill earlier in 2023. However, Andrade created problems from the opening moments of their fight. The former UFC strawweight champion dropped Dern late in the first round and continued her pressure in the second round. Andrade scored multiple knockdowns before finishing the fight with strikes.The victory made Andrade the first fighter to finish Dern inside the Octagon. It was a major setback for Dern, who had built her reputation as one of the most dangerous submission specialists in women’s MMA.The loss also extended a difficult period against elite competition.Before facing Andrade, Dern had suffered defeats against Marina Rodriguez in Oct. 2021 and Yan Xiaonan in Oct. 2022. Thoselosses showed Dern needed to make changes if she wanted to compete for a championship.After the Andrade setback,Mackenzie Dern focused on improving her overall game. Her Brazilian jiu-jitsu remained her biggest weapon, but she continued working on her striking and fight strategy.She returned to action on May 25, 2024, against Loopy Godínez at UFC Fight Night. Article Title: Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "Don't call me an icon. I'm just a mother trying to…" - a timeless lesson on humility, compassion and leading through kindness
Article Text:
Quote of the Day by Princess Diana

Quote of the day by Princess Diana

"Don't call me an icon. I'm just a mother trying to help"

Understanding the meaning behind Princess Diana’s quote

Why humility can actually strengthen leadership

Why kindness tends to leave a deeper legacy than fame does

Why family can remain the greatest priority, even for someone this famous

Why real service matters more than being recognised for it

Why being authentic tends to build genuine trust

A note on Princess Diana's humanitarian legacy

Other memorable quotes by Princess Diana

"Carry out a random act of kindness, with no expectation of reward, safe in the knowledge that one day someone might do the same for you."

"Everyone needs to be valued. Everyone has the potential to give something back."

"I want to walk into a room, be it a hospice for the dying or a hospital for sick children, and feel that I am needed. I want to do, not just to be."

"Only do what your heart tells you."

"I don't go by the rule book... I lead from the heart, not the head."

Why it remains close to people's hearts

History tends to remember extraordinary people through grand titles, icons, legends, symbols of change. Plenty of those same people saw themselves very differently. Princess Diana put that gap plainly. "Don't call me an icon," she said. "I'm just a mother trying to help." Known across the world as the People's Princess, she consistently pushed back against the pedestal people kept trying to place her on, insisting instead that she was simply someone trying, however imperfectly, to do some genuine good in the time she actually had.Her compassion, warmth and willingness to connect with people facing illness, poverty and social stigma reshaped public attitudes toward humanitarian work, leaving a legacy defined not only by global admiration but also by empathy, kindness and a deeply personal commitment to helping others.Diana is expressing real discomfort with being placed on a pedestal purely because of her position or public image. She was not asking to be admired for her status. She wanted to be seen simply as someone doing her genuine best to care for her children and help people who actually needed it. The quote carries two values running right through it, humility and compassion, both suggesting that actions were always going to matter more than whatever label the public happened to attach to her.Leadership usually gets associated with authority or influence. Diana showed a different route entirely, leading through empathy instead. By actually listening to people, comforting those going through real hardship, and treating everyone she met with genuine dignity, she earned a kind of respect that went well beyond anything royal tradition alone could have produced. Humility lets a leader connect with people on a human level rather than purely through status.Titles and public recognition tend to fade with time. Genuine acts of kindness tend to stick around considerably longer than any of that ever does. Diana became known specifically for spending real time with hospital patients, comforting children directly, and physically embracing people who were often stigmatised or simply overlooked by everyone else, including her famous, deliberate handshake with an AIDS patient in 1987, at a time when public fear around the disease was severe enough that many people avoided any physical contact with patients entirely. Her legacy has lasted largely because of how she genuinely made people feel, not simply because of her title.Despite carrying enormous public responsibility, Diana repeatedly described motherhood as the single most important part of her own life, above her royal duties, above her public profile, above almost everything else people associated her with. This quote reflects that directly, suggesting personal relationships often matter more than professional achievement, however impressive that achievement happens to look from the outside. Success tends to carry more real meaning once it is balanced with genuine love, care and responsibility toward the people closest to you.Plenty of people quietly hope their own efforts will eventually be noticed. Diana's words suggest something different entirely, that helping people should never actually depend on receiving praise for it in the first place. Acts of service become considerably more meaningful once they come from genuine concern rather than any hope of public recognition. Real influence tends to grow naturally out of consistent kindness rather than from any deliberate campaign to be noticed.People are naturally drawn to authenticity wherever they actually find it in someone, especially someone as heavily scrutinised as Diana was. Diana's willingness to speak openly about her own struggles, including her documented struggle with postnatal depression, made her genuinely relatable to millions of people who had never met her in person. She never really tried to appear flawless. She simply embraced her own humanity instead, and that openness is really what built the trust that made her so widely loved in the first place.Princess Diana used her public platform to support numerous humanitarian causes throughout her life. She helped raise real awareness about HIV and AIDS at a time when serious misconceptions and stigma were still widespread, visited hospitals around the world, and became an internationally recognised advocate for banning anti-personnel landmines, walking personally through partially cleared minefields in Angola and Bosnia to draw attention to the issue. Her compassion and her genuine willingness to connect personally with people from every walk of life remain central to how she is remembered today, decades after her death.Modern culture tends to celebrate popularity, influence and public image above almost everything else. Diana's message offers a genuinely different measure of what actually counts as success. Rather than asking how famous someone becomes, it asks how much genuine good they actually bring into the lives of the people around them, quietly, without needing anyone to notice or applaud it. That lesson applies just as much to parents, teachers, volunteers and community leaders as it ever did to a princess. Long after headlines and honours have faded, kindness and genuine concern for other people are usually what actually define a meaningful life.
Article Summary: Quote of the day by Princess Diana: "Don't call me an icon. I'm just a mother trying to help" The quote carries two values running right through it, humility and compassion. Diana is expressing real discomfort with being placed on a pedestal purely because of her position or public image.

She had shared that doctors found tumors in her lungs, and earlier this year also revealed tumors in her stomach. Even after a former oncologist suggested transitioning to end-of-life care, she sought a second opinion and decided to keep exploring additional treatment options.She also celebrated a personal milestone during that period by walking the runway at Miami Swim Week after receiving clearance from a new specialist to travel. Article Title: ECB 'unhappy' as Ireland defy England's policy, host Afghanistan for ODI series
Article Text:
Afghanistan's Rashid Khan. (AP)
