The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) is reportedly unhappy with Cricket Ireland for hosting Afghanistan in a five-match ODI series, even though England continue to play Afghanistan in ICC tournaments.The five-match ODI series between Ireland and Afghanistan began on Wednesday in Bready. According to a report in The Guardian, Ireland's decision to host Afghanistan could affect its future cricket ties with England.Ireland's move has put its relationship with the ECB under strain. England have refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan because of the Taliban regime's restrictions on women's rights.The ECB's stance is based on concerns over what its chair, Richard Thompson, has described as the Taliban's "gender apartheid".However, England continue to face Afghanistan in ICC events, where tournament points and titles are at stake.The ECB's policy is supported by the UK government, but Cricket Ireland has taken a different approach. Ireland has built close ties with the Afghanistan Cricket Board and is hosting five ODIs this month.Under a reciprocal arrangement, Ireland will tour the United Arab Emirates in March next year to play Afghanistan in one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is.England previously played one-off Tests against Ireland at Lord's before the home Ashes series in 2019 and 2023. Next year, however, England have chosen to play Bangladesh in a warm-up Test instead.England's men's team also faced Afghanistan in the Champions Trophy in Lahore last year.While the ECB does not schedule bilateral matches against Afghanistan, it has supported Afghan women cricketers in other ways. This summer, it organised a tour of England for the Afghan Refugee Women's team and invited them to attend the T20 World Cup final at Lord's.Most members of the Afghanistan women's team fled the country after the Taliban returned to power in 2021 and banned women's sport. Many of the players later settled in Australia.Afghanistan remain the only ICC Full Member without a women's cricket programme, but the ICC has not suspended them.Australia, South Africa and New Zealand have also refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan. Ireland, however, has joined the West Indies, Zimbabwe and the four Asian ICC Full Members in continuing bilateral cricket with Afghanistan.The ECB's relationship with Cricket Ireland has already been under pressure. England declined an invitation to take part in the proposed Euro Nations Cup next year, which would also feature Scotland, the Netherlands and Italy, citing a packed international schedule.England's men's team played a three-match T20I series in Ireland last September, but the ECB sent a second-string squad. No further men's matches between the two teams are currently scheduled.England's women's team, however, will host Ireland in a three-match ODI series next month.
Article Summary: England and Wales Cricket Board unhappy with Cricket Ireland for hosting Afghanistan in a five-match ODI series. England have refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan because of the Taliban regime's restrictions on women's rights. ECB's stance is based on concerns over what its chair, Richard Thompson, has described as the Taliban's "gender apartheid" England continue to face Afghanistan in ICC events where tournament points and titles are at stake.

Article Title: ‘I am still living’: Georgina Rodríguez answers ‘body-shaming’ critics as Cristiano Ronaldo’s private words come to light
Article Text:
‘I am still living’: Georgina Rodríguez answers ‘body-shaming’ critics as Cristiano Ronaldo’s private words come to light

Cristiano Ronaldo’s fiancée Georgina Rodríguez explains why she refuses to let body-shaming define her

Georgina Rodríguez says she exercises for happiness, not to meet society’s expectations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Recent photos of Cristiano Ronaldo ’s fiancée Georgina Rodríguez enjoying time on a boat led to a wave of comments about her appearance on social media. While many fans defended her, others criticised her body, prompting the model to share a personal message on Instagram . Instead of responding to individual comments, Rodríguez spoke about motherhood, confidence and why she refuses to let strangers decide how she should feel about herself. She also revealed what Ronaldo told her during a private conversation, saying his words reminded her that her value is far greater than physical appearance. Her post focused on accepting change, raising confident daughters and rejecting unrealistic beauty standards.Rodríguez said she understands that her body will continue to change and believes that should never be seen as something negative. As the mother of six children, including three daughters she shares with Ronaldo, she said she wants her children to grow up knowing that self-worth should never depend on appearance or the opinions of strangers.She wrote:“My body will change, just like every woman’s body changes. And I hope it continues to do so for many years, because that will mean I am still living. I am the mother of six wonderful children, three of whom are girls who will one day become great women. And if there is one thing I want to teach them - along with Cris, whom I feel deeply proud of for the values he passes on as a father and as a man - it is that a person’s worth can never depend on their physical appearance or the opinions of strangers.That small dose of positive psychology that I try to give them every day also helps me continue finding my way in a world filled with so much illusion.”Rodríguez also shared that the criticism upset her because people often judge her only through her public image. She said Ronaldo reminded her that the qualities that truly matter cannot be measured by appearance.She wrote:“And he replied: ‘You don’t make a living from your image. You make a living from who you are. A perfect woman. Beautiful, with an amazing body, a mother, a good person, successful, and someone who lives life with love. What more could you want? It’s normal that people envy you. And we talked about many other things too.’”Rodríguez also spoke about how the same discussion returns every summer, with people once again focusing on her body. She questioned who decides what the “right” body should look like and rejected the idea that happiness has a certain size. She said going to the gym is something she does because it makes her feel good, not because she wants to meet anyone else’s expectations.She continued:“The curious thing is that this happens every summer. Every year, my body becomes news again. And then I ask myself… where is the standard? Who decides what the “right” body is? Do we really still believe that happiness has a size? I work out because it makes me happy… I love my curves.I love the freedom of living in the body I choose.The body that supports me, that has allowed me to embrace, create life, fall down, and get back up again. A body that deserves respect, love, and gratitude in all its forms.”Georgina Rodríguez ended her message by saying she is thankful for everything her body has carried her through, from motherhood to life’s challenges. She said real success comes from inner peace, good health and meaningful relationships, not from trying to match unrealistic beauty standards.
Article Summary: Georgina Rodríguez says she exercises for happiness, not to meet society’s expectations. She said she wants her children to grow up knowing that self-worth should never depend on appearance or the opinions of strangers. Her post focused on accepting change, raising confident daughters and rejecting unrealistic beauty standards.

Article Title: What happened to Cowboys TE Princeton Fant? Latest injury update after scary training camp incident

Dallas Cowboys confirm Princeton Fant suffered a season-ending ACL and partial MCL injury

The Dallas Cowboys received tough news from training camp after tight end Princeton Fant suffered a serious knee injury during practice in Oxnard, California. What initially looked like a scary moment on the field quickly turned into a major setback for both the player and the team.Princeton Fant's injury occurred during a team rushing drill. Fant tried to set up a block when a running back clipped his knee. Trainers rushed to him immediately, helped him off the field, and later took him to the locker room on a cart. For a player trying to earn a bigger role, the moment changed everything within seconds.Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed after practice that Princeton Fant tore his ACL and partially tore his MCL. He told reporters in Oxnard that Fant will miss the entire season. The team plans to wait until the MCL settles down before moving forward with surgery.Schottenheimer sounded disappointed for the player more than anything else. While speaking to reporters after practice, he said, “Really disappointed for him, for everything that he’s put into this.” He also told Fant that his story is far from over and added that doctors believe he has a strong chance to make a full recovery.That stance carried extra meaning because Fant has already dealt with a major knee injury. According to reports, he sustained a similar injury in high school in Tennessee, which caused him to miss most of his junior and senior seasons. That earlier setback forced him to rebuild his career long before he reached the NFL, so this latest injury becomes another difficult chapter in a journey that has already included major adversity.Princeton Fant entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent from Tennessee and has spent the last three seasons with the Dallas Cowboys. Most of his work came on special teams and as a depth tight end. He has played in 11 career games and has not recorded a reception, but coaches valued his blocking ability and physical style.That is why this injury hurts more than the stat line suggests. Princeton Fant entered camp with a real opportunity to strengthen his place on the roster behind Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker. Coaches viewed him as one of the better blockers in the tight end room, and that role mattered in both the running game and special teams.Now the Dallas Cowboys must reshuffle the position group. Brevyn Spann-Ford, Michael Trigg, and DJ Rogers should receive more reps during the rest of camp and the preseason. Trigg and Rogers, both undrafted rookies, suddenly have a much bigger chance to prove they can contribute as blockers and special teams players.The frightening scene on the practice field created immediate concern, and the official diagnosis confirmed the worst fear. Princeton Fant’s season is over, and the Dallas Cowboys lose an experienced depth player just as training camp competition begins to intensify. For Fant, the focus now shifts from making the roster to tackling a long rehab process and working his way back onto an NFL field.
Article Summary: Dallas Cowboys confirm Princeton Fant suffered a season-ending ACL and partial MCL injury. Fant entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent from Tennessee and has spent the last three seasons with the Dallas Cowboys. Brevyn Spann-Ford, Michael Trigg, and DJ Rogers should receive more reps.

While the dismissal does not end the broader dispute, it suggests both sides are now attempting to settle matters outside the California court system.Anamaria Goltes filed documents on Monday asking a Los Angeles judge to dismiss her child support petition without prejudice, according to TMZ. The move allows the issue to be revisited in the future if necessary, but for now reflects an effort to reach an agreement away from the courtroom."I am withdrawing my Petition for Child Support with the specific intention of resolving this matter amicably and by a mutual agreement which is in the best interests of our children," Goltes stated in court documents obtained by TMZ.Her decision follows Luka Doncic's legal challenge to the California filing. Through attorney Laura Wasser, the Los Angeles Lakers star reportedly argued that the petition lacked legal grounds because the children have been living in Slovenia rather than California. Court filings also claimed Doncic encouraged Goltes to relocate to California with their daughters, but she chose to remain in Slovenia, where the children have lived since May.The legal process, however, has not been entirely straightforward. Sources familiar with the situation told the outlet that custody proceedings remain active under the jurisdiction of Slovenian courts.Doncic and Goltes were together for approximately a decade before ending their engagement, with reports indicating that long-distance challenges played a role in the separation. Article Title: French trans basketball star Julie Tétart hopes to join WNBA following Sophie Cunningham’s controversial statement
Article Text:
Julie Tétart. Image via: Getty Images

Julie Tétart is eyeing a move to the WNBA

Julie Tétart dominated France's Ligue Féminine 2

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Julie Tétart's WNBA hopes gain spotlight amid Sophie Cunningham's comments

Julie Tétart, the French transgender basketball player who led her league in scoring and rebounding this past season, says she would accept a WNBA contract if one came her way. The comment surfaced as the league continues wrestling with a separate controversy involving Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, whose remarks opposing transgender participation in women's sports sparked protests, a suspension, and White House attention over the past several weeks.Tétart, who plays center for Monaco Basket Association in France's Ligue Féminine 2, told reporters she wasn't holding her breath but wouldn't turn down the opportunity either.Tétart's numbers from the 2025-26 LF2 season made the question worth asking. She averaged roughly 21 points and 20 rebounds per game, leading the league in both categories while playing at 6-foot-3. Despite that production, she was passed over for MVP, though she still collected Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, and Domestic Player of the Year honors.Asked directly whether she'd consider trying out for a WNBA roster, Tétart didn't dismiss it. "I won't say no," she said. She followed that by noting the realistic obstacles facing a 34-year-old crossing over from a second-tier European league, pointing out that plenty of players in the WNBA are simply better equipped for that level. “But you have to be realistic: I'm old, and there are far better players than me!" Tétart told OutKick.Her dominance wasn't limited to a strong statistical average. During one March game, Tétart posted 21 points and 30 rebounds, setting a new league rebounding record and breaking her own previous mark. Such production is part of why French trans advocacy groups pushed back hard when she was left off the league's MVP ballot, a decision that also excluded fellow trans player Aurore Pautou despite her own strong season.Tétart addressed the possibility of a WNBA future carefully, calling it a longtime aspiration shared by any young female basketball player, but adding that circumstances outside the sport make it unlikely. She pointed to broader political conditions in the United States, without going into detail, as the sticking point rather than anything about the league itself.The timing put Tétart's comments squarely inside an ongoing WNBA debate. Cunningham, a seventh-year guard for the Fever, drew national attention after telling ESPN she supports keeping transgender athletes out of girls' and women's sports, framing her stance as protective rather than hostile. She stood by the comments the next day, telling reporters, "I said what I said. I think it's kind of common sense."Not everyone in the league agreed. Fever head coach Stephanie White pushed back on framing exclusion as any kind of solution, saying, "I don't ever believe that exclusion is an answer," while acknowledging she didn't consider herself well-versed in the underlying science. Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve went further, later telling reporters, "I come from a space of inclusion," and wearing a shirt reading "Trans Kids Belong" during a game against Indiana.Whether Tétart ever gets an actual roster offer remains an open question. For now, her answer stands on record, and the league's ongoing debate over transgender inclusion shows no sign of settling before training camps open.
Article Summary: Julie Tétart led France's Ligue Féminine 2 in scoring and rebounding this season. The 34-year-old center says she would accept a WNBA contract if one came her way. The comment surfaced as the league continues wrestling with a separate controversy involving Sophie Cunningham.

Article Title: Meet Nathan Thomas: 18-year-old Florida teen becomes the world's youngest male professor after breaking a 306-year-old record
Article Text:
How Nathan Thomas became the world's youngest male professor

Image: CBS Miami

An extraordinary academic journey

A passion for engineering and teaching

Looking beyond engineering

An inspiration for young learners

At an age when many students are just beginning university, Nathan Thomas had already stepped into the classroom as a college professor. The Florida native earned a place in the Guinness World Records after becoming the world's youngest male professor at just 18 years and 346 days old, breaking a record that had stood for 306 years. Thomas joined Miami Dade College as an engineering instructor, where he teaches students who are often close to his own age. His remarkable academic journey, which began with enrolling in college at the age of 10, has now made him one of the youngest educators ever to teach at the higher education level. His journey stands out not only for the record itself but for what it represents, a reminder that intellectual growth does not always follow a fixed timeline, and that curiosity, nurtured early, can open doors. His achievement highlights how exceptional talent, supported by dedication and opportunity, can challenge conventional expectations about age and redefine what is possible in education.Beyond setting a historic record, Thomas has become an inspiration for young learners around the world, demonstrating that passion for knowledge, continuous learning and confidence in one's abilities can overcome traditional barriers and create opportunities that many people might consider impossible.Nathan Thomas officially became the world's youngest male professor when he accepted an engineering teaching position at Miami Dade College at the age of 18 years and 346 days. Guinness World Records confirmed that he surpassed the record previously held by Scottish mathematician Colin Maclaurin, who became a professor at the age of 19 in 1717. The achievement ended a record that had remained unbeaten for more than three centuries.Thomas began teaching COP 2270: C for Engineers at Miami Dade College in August 2023. The course introduces engineering students to the fundamentals of C programming and computational problem-solving. Many of his students are around the same age as him, but Thomas believes age matters far less than a willingness to learn. He has said that everyone enters the classroom with the same goal of gaining knowledge and improving their skills. His appointment also demonstrates that expertise and dedication, rather than age alone, can earn respect in higher education.Thomas displayed exceptional academic ability from an early age. At just 10 years old, he dual-enrolled at Miami Dade College while continuing his school education. By the age of 14, he had transferred to Florida International University, where he completed both bachelor's and master's degrees in electrical engineering with honours. His accelerated academic path eventually led him back to Miami Dade College, this time as a faculty member rather than a student.Coming from a family of engineers, Thomas developed an interest in mathematics and science at a young age. He has credited his mother with helping him understand mathematical concepts in ways that made learning enjoyable. He says the most rewarding part of teaching is watching students grasp ideas that once seemed difficult, describing those moments as just as satisfying as solving engineering problems himself.While continuing to teach, Thomas is also pursuing a Juris Doctor degree at the University of Miami School of Law, with an expected graduation in 2028. He hopes to combine his engineering background with legal expertise by specialising in intellectual property law, particularly in areas involving science, technology, engineering and mathematics. According to Thomas, the structured problem-solving skills he developed through engineering have proved valuable in his legal studies. As emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence continue to reshape industries, expertise spanning both engineering and intellectual property law is expected to play an increasingly important role in protecting innovation. By bridging engineering and law, he hopes to contribute to the protection of innovation in rapidly evolving fields driven by science and technology.Nathan Thomas's achievement demonstrates how determination, curiosity and a passion for learning can open extraordinary opportunities at a young age. From entering college as a child to becoming the world's youngest male professor and breaking a 306-year-old Guinness World Record, his journey has inspired students and educators alike. As he continues balancing teaching with law school, Thomas hopes to contribute to both education and innovation while encouraging others to pursue ambitious goals regardless of age.
Article Summary: Nathan Thomas became the world's youngest male professor at the age of 18 years and 346 days. The record had been held by Scottish mathematician Colin Maclaurin, who was 19 in 1717. Thomas is also pursuing a Juris Doctor degree at the University of Miami School of Law.

Article Title: Polish swimmer becomes the first person to swim from Sweden to Poland across the Baltic Sea in 55 hours
Article Text:
Image: AOL News

A historic 160-kilometre swim completed on the fifth attempt

Battling exhaustion, cold water and hallucinations for more than two days

Years of preparation and a swim that also raised money for charity

In a historic feat, Bartłomiej Kubkowski, an ultra-swimmer from Poland, became the first person to successfully swim across the Baltic Sea from Sweden to Poland without any physical help. Making it to the other side in 55 hours and 10 minutes, Kubkowski completed the 160-kilometre trek under very difficult conditions. Swimming through the cold water and fighting the current, as well as sleep and physical fatigue, he managed to accomplish something no one had done on this route before.The historic swim began on Friday from the Swedish coastal village of Kaseberga and ended on Sunday evening when Kubkowski reached Dziwnow on Poland's Baltic coast. Throughout the journey, a support boat accompanied him with food, hydration and safety monitoring, but he was never allowed to touch it. According to Euronews, the exhausted yet triumphant swimmer became the first person to conquer the challenging Baltic crossing entirely under his own power after spending more than two continuous days in open water.Kubkowski began his journey from Kaseberga on Sweden's southern coast on Friday and arrived at Dziwnów in Poland roughly 55 hours later after swimming approximately 160 kilometres across the Baltic Sea.The crossing had strict rules: although accompanied by a support boat for navigation, food and hydration, he was not allowed to touch the vessel at any point. To have the achievement officially recognised, he also had to leave the water under his own strength, a requirement he successfully fulfilled.The achievement came after years of perseverance. Kubkowski first attempted the crossing in 2022 but had to abandon it after covering 115 kilometres. His closest attempt came in 2025, when he swam around 159 kilometres before extreme exhaustion forced him to stop only a short distance from the Polish coast. This fifth expedition finally turned his long-held ambition into reality.Swimming the Baltic Sea implied coping with the cold water, unpredictable weather, and physical exhaustion without sleeping at all. Kubkowski felt extremely tired, confused, and even hallucinated after more than 50 hours in the water; these difficulties were foreseen by his team from their experience in other similar attempts.During the swimming session, his safety was strictly observed while providing him with food and water with the help of long poles, without letting him touch the boat. Despite getting lost and being unable to concentrate sometimes, Kubkowski managed to finish the last kilometres of his swim on the shore of Poland. Euronews reported that he later admitted he was simply too exhausted to fully comprehend what he had achieved.Kubkowski's historic crossing was not just a sporting milestone but also a charitable mission. The swim raised hundreds of thousands of Polish zlotys for the Cancer Fighters Foundation, supporting people battling cancer.Kubkowski was not only a professional swimmer but also had the title of being the world record for the greatest distance swim in a pool within 24 hours. He trained for months through rigorous endurance sessions and night swims to be able to accomplish his feat, which has brought him much fame not only in Poland but also in other countries of Europe.
Article Summary: Bartłomiej Kubkowski, an ultra-swimmer from Poland, became the first person to successfully swim across the Baltic Sea from Sweden to Poland without any physical help. The historic swim began on Friday from the Swedish coastal village of Kaseberga and ended on Sunday evening when Kubkowski reached Dziwnow on Poland's Baltic coast. The swim raised hundreds of thousands of Polish zlotys for the Cancer Fighters Foundation.

Article Title: First total solar eclipse of 2026 falls on August 12: What makes it special, the best places to watch, and what you must never do
Article Text:
Representative image

Where the August 12 total solar eclipse will be visible

What makes this eclipse different from the 2024 one



How to watch the total solar eclipse live online



Solar eclipse safety: What not to do while watching



The Moon will slide fully across the Sun on the evening of August 12, dropping a narrow band of Europe into darkness for a little over a minute in some places and close to two in others. It is the first total solar eclipse anywhere on Earth since April 2024, and the first to cross the Iberian Peninsula in more than a century. Spain is the headline act here, simply because it is the only densely populated stretch of land the shadow touches.Totality begins over the Arctic, sweeps across eastern Greenland and western Iceland, clips a sliver of northeastern Portugal at Montesinho Natural Park, and then runs west to east across northern Spain. Everywhere else in Europe, and a chunk of North America, gets a partial bite out of the Sun instead.In Spain, León, Burgos, Valladolid, Santander, Bilbao, Zaragoza, Valencia and Palma all sit in the path of totality, with peak around 8:32-8:33 pm CEST. Madrid misses it by a hair at 99 percent obscuration. Iceland's western coast, including Reykjavík and Ísafjörður, sees totality earlier at 5:48 pm GMT, though Látrabjarg holds it longest.Elsewhere, Dublin gets 94 percent, Paris 92, London 91. North America does far worse. New York manages 9 percent, Washington DC just 4, and Chicago a rounding error at 0.1 percent. St John's in Newfoundland is the continent's best seat at 53 percent. India sees nothing, since the eclipse happens well past midnight IST.Two things. It coincides with lunar perigee, so the Moon appears slightly larger than usual and totality stretches longer than it otherwise would. It also lands on the Perseid meteor shower, which peaks the same night. Watch the eclipse at sunset, then wait for the sky to fill with meteors.ESA is streaming it free on YouTube and ESA Web TV from 19:30 to 20:45 CEST, hosted by space scientist Dame Dr Maggie Aderin. The main feed comes from the Observatorio Astrofísico de Javalambre in Teruel, where 1 minute 21 seconds of totality hits at 20:31 CEST, with additional feeds from León and Frómista as cloud insurance. ESA is also running a free public event at the Palacio de Exposiciones y Congresos in León, mostly in Spanish.Do not look at the Sun without certified eclipse glasses at any point outside totality. Sunglasses do not work. Binoculars and telescopes without solar filters are worse than nothing. The American Astronomical Society maintains a list of approved viewers. Shooting it? Your lens needs a solar filter too. The safest option costs nothing: a pinhole projector, or a kitchen colander held above the ground, which throws dozens of tiny crescent Suns onto the pavement.
Article Summary: The Moon will slide fully across the Sun on the evening of August 12, dropping a narrow band of Europe into darkness for a little over a minute in some places and close to two in others. It is the first total solar eclipse anywhere on Earth since April 2024, and the first to cross the Iberian Peninsula in more than a century.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture

A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. Article Title: Lakshmi Yojana rollout stumbles as Delhi women run into registration hassles
Article Text:
Delhi’s Lakshmi Yojana hits roadblocks as women struggle to even register (AI image used for representational purpose only).

Lakshmi plan applicants run into regn roadblock

OI

Getting letter from MP/MLA major challenge.

TOI





NEW DELHI: Delhi govt's Lakshmi Yojana, launched Augt 1, promises Rs 2,500 a month for eligible women. But many are getting stuck at the first level - registration.The signature of an MP or legislator, hunt for a decade-old address proof, repeated trips to cyber cafes to fill forms online and no option to correct mistakes on submitted forms have turned the scheme into a process that many can ill-afford.According to senior officials, this is Delhi govt's only scheme that makes the signature of an MP or MLA mandatory for registration.To understand exactly how accessible the registration process is for an ordinary applicant, TOI visited the offices of six legislators.visited the offices of BJP MLAs Shikha Rai (Greater Kailash), Tarvinder Singh Marwah (Jangpura), Kapil Mishra (Karawal Nagar), Parvesh Verma (New Delhi), AAP MLA Atishi (Kalkaji) and BJP MP Manoj Tiwari (North East Delhi).Women, accompanied in many cases by children and husbands, carried filled forms and documents. Some waited for the representative’s signature and many returned empty-handed because of incomplete forms, missing documents or confusion over the process.The registration process itself emerged as one of the biggest bottlenecks. Several women reached MLA offices carrying only their Aadhaar cards and other documents, believing they could fill the form there.Instead, they were told the form had to be submitted online first before they could seek the MLA’s signature.Others relied on cyber cafés, where the application often took close to an hour because of multiple document uploads. If a mistake has been made while filling the form and it has been submitted, the option to edit or correct the mistake is not available at present.Adding to their difficulties was the requirement of proving 10 years of residence in Delhi. Many women said they had replaced old voter identity cards or lost older records over the years. Despite living in Delhi for decades, they were unsure how they would establish eligibility.At around 11.50am Monday, five to six families, mostly women, waited in the basement office of BJP MLA Shikha Rai in Greater Kailash, clutching printouts of their applications. Many had taken leave from work, while others had brought their children along because there was no one to look after them.Office staff scrutinised every application before accepting it. Applicants whose forms were complete were asked to return the following day because the MLA was not present to sign them. Most others were asked to correct errors before they could proceed. “We don’t know how to use smartphones.People told us we would get the form here. We came early in the morning, but after reaching here we were told to first fill the form online and then return with a printed copy for the MLA’s signature,” said Suman Singh, a resident of Chirag Delhi.For 53-year-old Tulsi, the problem came after she had already completed the online application. “I came with my daughter only to get the MLA’s signature, but we were told there was a mistake in the application. We had selected the wrong assembly constituency. There is no option to edit the form. We have been told the application must first be deleted and then filled again,” said Tulsi, whose husband drives an autorickshaw.At the office of AAP MLA Atishi, the queue looked different. Most people waiting were men completing applications on behalf of their wives or mothers. Drivers, restaurant workers and small shopkeepers stood in line with bundles of documents. Sumit Kumar , who had come to submit his wife’s application, said the process was smooth because all his documents were in order. “I filled the form online and brought all the required documents. The office verified everything, got the form signed and now I only have to upload it on the portal,” he said. But not everyone was able to move ahead.Shabnam Khan , who accompanied her mother, said her mother’s application was completed without difficulty. Her own application, however, was held up because she could not produce the required ten-year address proof after her address changed after she got married two years ago.On Tuesday, BJP MLA Tarvinder Singh Marwah’s office in Jangpura saw a steady stream of applicants submitting completed forms for signatures. Staff told applicants they would receive a phone call once their signed forms were ready for collection.Pinky Singh, who had submitted her application on Aug 1, said she received a call while on her way to pick up her child from school informing her that the signed documents were ready. “Earlier family members could collect the forms, but now only the applicant is allowed to take them,” she said.At BJP MP Manoj Tiwari’s office, staff were helping applicants with the registration process. Those travelling from far were told they could send documents over WhatsApp, after which the office would facilitate the signature and upload the signed documents on the portal.Around noon Wednesday, Delhi minister and New Delhi MLA Parvesh Verma’s office had no queue, but staff was assisting applicants with documentation and registration.Few applicants reached the Karawal Nagar office of minister Kapil Mishra in heavy rain. Staff accepted only completed applications, while many women left without submitting their forms because they were either unsure about eligibility or did not have documents.Among them was Ridhina, whose husband has a pani-puri cart. With three children and no voter ID, she arrived hoping someone would explain whether she was eligible.“I came to understand whether I am eligible because my parents have passed away and I don’t have all the required documents. But the office was only accepting completed forms. I went back without any clarity,” she said.Mishra toldthat his office completed more than 4,000 applications so far. “Our immediate priority is to process and sign those forms first... In the coming days, we will also seek the support of councillors to assist applicants.Volunteers will be deployed in every ward to help people with document verification and the online application process, especially those who are not comfortable with technology,” Mishra said.He added that a facilitation centre has been set up at a banquet hall to help residents fill out the forms. “Gradually, we will expand this assistance so that more people can receive help with both online registration and document-related issues,” he said.Across offices, one concern repeatedly surfaced: many women were struggling to produce the documents required to prove their eligibility, particularly decade-old proof of residence.The second was that there seemed to be no recourse if incorrect information had been filled in the registration form – something that many women are finding out only when they visit MP/MLA offices.Elected representatives, except Mishra, did not respond to calls or messages regarding the challenges and pace of registration.According to a senior official in the department of women and child development, the option of editing a form after submission is being discussed with NIC, which developed the portal.
Article Summary: Delhi govt's Lakshmi Yojana promises Rs 2,500 a month for eligible women. But many are getting stuck at the first level - registration. The signature of an MP or legislator, hunt for a decade-old address proof, repeated trips to cyber cafes to fill forms online have turned the scheme into a process that many can ill-afford.
